title: Water Crisis Hits Srinagar’s Press Colony for Second Consecutive Day - Kashmir Life
full_text:
SRINAGAR: A shortage of tap water for the past two days has disrupted daily operations at Srinagar’s Press Colony, causing inconvenience to journalists and other media professionals working in the area.
A group of journalists said the shortage had affected their daily routines, particularly those who spend long hours in newsrooms. Several journalists have been forced to visit neighbouring areas to fetch water for their basic needs.
Fayaz Ahmad, a local journalist, said the shortage had caused considerable difficulties for media professionals.
“We are facing a lot of problems due to the water shortage. We have been going to other areas to fetch water for the past few days,” he said.
Meanwhile, an official of the Jal Shakti (PHE) Department, Kashmir, told Kashmir Life that the department was working to restore the water supply.
“The supply is low, yes, and we are working on it. It may be restored by late this evening or tomorrow,” the official said.
The continued shortage has raised concerns among media professionals, who have urged the authorities concerned to take immediate steps to ensure a regular water supply to the Press Colony.
